title: Preferential trade agreements: How businesses can adapt | World Economic Forum
gist: A WEF–PwC briefing argues preferential trade agreements are underused: about 4% of global merchandise trade eligible for preferential treatment still moves on MFN terms, and mapping sourcing, production and market access against agreements builds optionality and resilience beyond tariff savings.

insights.claim: WTO analysis shows around 4% of global merchandise trade is eligible for preferential treatment but continues under most-favoured-nation terms, and one company in the briefing saved more than $16 million in just over a year by switching to PTA preferences.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Unclaimed preferences are a cheap, immediate margin lever for importers and exporters.
insights.locator: Yet opportunities are still being missed

insights.claim: Newer preferential agreements increasingly cover services, digital trade, data flows, sustainability and energy cooperation, making them relevant to sourcing, investment and market-access decisions beyond tariff reduction.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Trade-agreement membership increasingly shapes where firms locate digital and services operations.

insights.claim: Because companies cannot establish new suppliers, production footprints or customer markets overnight, assessing alternative trade corridors and PTA opportunities in advance improves their ability to switch suppliers, adjust routes and preserve continuity when conditions change.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Firms that pre-map agreement networks should adapt faster to tariff or disruption shocks.
insights.locator: Using trade agreements to build resilience

insights.claim: Friendshoring and economic-security considerations are contributing to a growing network of bilateral, regional and sector-specific agreements that companies can map against their supplier, production and market networks.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Trade fragmentation is producing more, not fewer, agreements — a mapping task for corporate strategy.

insights.claim: Executives should bring PTA analysis into sourcing, manufacturing, investment and market-entry decisions upfront rather than after the decisions are made, starting by measuring how much eligible trade claims preferences.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Operational recommendation: integrate trade-rule analysis early in network design.
insights.locator: Building options before they are needed

insights.claim: The Panama Canal connects 180 maritime routes, 1,920 ports and 170 countries and facilitates approximately 5% of global trade, making Panama's logistics zones and industrial clusters more central as trade becomes less predictable.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Panama's exposure to global trade flows makes it a logistics beneficiary and a chokepoint risk.
